notes:
I found sources for about half of these verses. Most of what I found covers vv. 31–34, 56 and 58. My search and fetch budget ran out before I could read anything verse by verse for vv. 35–55. Two pages also loaded without the commentary text: the full Enduring Word chapter page cut off around v. 11, and the Blue Letter Bible copy of Guzik showed only menus. Following your rules, I've left out verses I couldn't source rather than fill them in myself.

## 1. Traditional reading, verse by verse

**v. 31**
- **Guzik (Enduring Word):** If we will be Jesus' disciples, we *must* abide in His word. There is no other way. He also notes that Jesus called men to abide in *His* word. In the mouth of anyone other than Jesus, these words would be absurd. — https://blueletterbible.org/comm/guzik_david/studyguide2017-jhn/jhn-8.cfm
- **Ellicott:** Jesus who reads the heart has no confidence in this momentary conviction. He links this to the shallow faith of John 2:23–25 and 6:66. — https://biblehub.com/john/8-31.htm
- **Cambridge Bible:** John switches from "believed on Him" in v. 30 to the weaker "believed Him" here, as if to prepare us for the collapse of their faith. Vincent's Word Studies says the same: their faith was only beginning. — https://biblehub.com/commentaries/john/8-31.htm
- **Gill:** "My word" means the Gospel. To continue in it is to hold it fast and not be moved by Satan's temptations, by deceivers, or by persecution. — https://www.studylight.org/commentary/john/8-31.html

**v. 32**
- **GotQuestions:** The freedom Jesus offers is a *spiritual* freedom from the bondage of sin. — https://www.gotquestions.org/the-truth-will-set-you-free.html
- **Guzik:** knowing the truth and being made free is the result of abiding in the word of Jesus. — https://blueletterbible.org/comm/guzik_david/studyguide2017-jhn/jhn-8.cfm
- **Pulpit Commentary, quoting Godet:** sin's hold on the heart rests on an illusion, and when truth shines, the spell breaks. — https://biblehub.com/john/8-31.htm

**v. 33**
- **Ligonier:** Jesus was talking about spiritual freedom, but the Pharisees took Him to mean physical slavery. — https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/abraham-was
- **Augustine:** their claim was false even in a physical sense. Joseph was sold, Israel served in Egypt, and they were paying tribute to Rome at that very moment. — https://www.newadvent.org/fathers/1701041.htm

**v. 34**
- **Ligonier:** Jesus made clear He meant slavery to sin, and the Pharisees picked up that He was calling them sinners. — https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/abraham-was
- **Augustine:** a human slave can run away, but the slave of sin can't, because he carries himself wherever he flees. — https://www.newadvent.org/fathers/1701041.htm

**vv. 35–36**
- **Augustine:** For he that endures to the end shall be saved. From this slavery we are freed by the Lord alone, the one who came without sin and paid the price with His own blood. — https://www.newadvent.org/fathers/1701041.htm

**vv. 37–40**
- **GotQuestions:** Jesus challenges their confidence in the flesh. They may be physically descended from Abraham, but they do not have Abraham's character. — https://www.gotquestions.org/before-Abraham-was-I-am.html

**vv. 52–53**
- **Ligonier:** when they demanded to know who He was, Jesus answered that He is greater than Abraham. — https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/abraham-was

**v. 56** (this verse has several competing readings; see section 2)
- **Calvin:** Abraham longed for me when I was absent, you despise me when I am present. — https://www.ccel.org/ccel/calvin/comment3/comm_vol34/htm/xiv.xi.htm
- **Barnes:** Abraham saw Christ's day prophetically, including a picture of His sacrificial death in the command to offer Isaac (Genesis 22). — https://www.studylight.org/bible/eng/web/john/8-56.html
- **Gill:** Abraham saw it by faith in the promise and in Isaac's birth (the name Isaac means "laughter"), and possibly saw Christ in human form in Genesis 18. — same page
- **Matthew Henry:** this may refer to Abraham's laughter of joy, not doubt, when God promised him a son (Genesis 17:17). — https://www.studylight.org/commentary/john/8-56.html
- **Spurgeon:** the first verb is a strong one ("he leaped forward"); the second is softer, a calm gladness. — https://www.spurgeon.org/resource-library/sermons/seeing-christs-day/

**v. 57**
- **Barnes:** their objection was that He wasn't yet 50, so He couldn't have seen Abraham. Jesus' answer must therefore refer to a nature other than His human one. — https://biblehub.com/commentaries/john/8-58.htm

**v. 58**
- **Ellicott:** There was a time when he was not. But there was never a time when the Son of God was not. — https://biblehub.com/john/8-58.htm
- **Pulpit Commentary:** the contrast is between "came into being" (used of Abraham) and "I am" (used of Jesus). The "I am" recalls Exodus 3:14 and Psalm 90. — same page
- **Jamieson-Fausset-Brown:** the point is not that Christ came into being before Abraham, as Arians claim, but that He never came into being at all. — https://biblehub.com/commentaries/john/8-58.htm
- **Ligonier:** the most explicit claim to deity that our Lord ever made. — https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/abraham-was
- **GotQuestions:** He does not say, "Before Abraham was, I was". He uses God's name from the burning bush. — https://www.gotquestions.org/before-Abraham-was-I-am.html
- **Gill:** the verse speaks of Christ's deity, eternity and unchangeableness. He rejects the readings that Christ existed only "in God's decree" or "before Abraham became father of many nations." — https://www.studylight.org/bible/eng/ubv/john/8-58.html

**v. 59**
- **GotQuestions:** none of His earlier claims made them pick up stones. Only the claim to be "I AM" did, which shows they heard it as blasphemy. — https://www.gotquestions.org/before-Abraham-was-I-am.html
- **Jamieson-Fausset-Brown:** they reacted the same way when He made Himself equal with God in John 5:18. — https://biblehub.com/commentaries/john/8-58.htm
- **Adam Clarke (cited by Guzik):** In all probability he rendered himself invisible. Others think He slipped away through the crowd. — https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/john-8/

## 2. Where traditions differ

**v. 31: what does lasting faith say about real faith?**
- **Reformed (Calvin):** continuing marks out true believers from hypocrites. Those who only boast of faith fall away, but believers persevere constantly to the end. — https://www.studylight.org/commentary/john/8-31.html
- **Baptist (Spurgeon):** Continuance is the sure test of the genuine believer. Jesus answers their weak faith with an "if," as a warning. — same page
- **Methodist/Wesleyan and Lutheran:** I didn't find their readings of this verse, so I can't present them.

**v. 56: when did Abraham "see"?**
- **Calvin:** he saw it in his lifetime, by faith and dimly. Calvin doubts the idea that Abraham saw it after death, and says Augustine wrongly took "day" to mean eternity. — https://www.ccel.org/ccel/calvin/calcom34.xiv.xi.html
- **Pulpit Commentary:** reports that Hofmann, Wordsworth and Westcott held that Abraham's hope came true after the Incarnation, as one of the glorified saints. Westcott thought the verb tense counts against joy in Paradise. — https://biblehub.com/commentaries/john/8-56.htm
- **Cambridge Bible:** reads the verse as showing the soul is conscious between death and judgment. — same page
- **Jamieson-Fausset-Brown:** Abraham met Christ as "the Angel of the Lord." — same page
- **Kelly (Brethren):** "my day" means the future day of Christ's glory. — https://www.studylight.org/commentary/john/8-56.html
- **Chuck Smith (Calvary Chapel):** possibly Abraham's meeting with Melchizedek. — same page

## 3. Other views

- **NET Bible notes (v. 58):** "I am!" is an explicit claim to deity. Not every "I am" in John points to Exodus 3:14, but this one clearly does, as the stoning in v. 59 shows. — https://classic.net.bible.org/verse.php?book=Joh&chapter=8&verse=58
- **Barclay (v. 56):** Jewish tradition held that Abraham had a vision of the Messiah, so Jesus was claiming to be the Messiah Abraham saw. — https://www.studylight.org/commentary/john/8-56.html
- **Rejected minority readings of v. 58:**
  - The Socinian Racovian Confession read it as "before Abram becomes Abraham (father of many nations), I am the Messiah." The Pulpit Commentary calls this "rabbinical trifling."
  - Beyschlag read it as an impersonal pre-existence in God's mind. — https://biblehub.com/john/8-58.htm
  - Benson notes that Grotius held a "pre-existent only in God's decree" view. — https://biblehub.com/commentaries/john/8-56.htm
- **Catholic (Augustine, v. 31):** as now you are believers, by so continuing you shall be beholders. He calls the Truth itself the Word of God, the only-begotten Son. He also ties freedom from the "fetters" inherited from Adam to the grace given infants at baptism. — https://www.newadvent.org/fathers/1701041.htm
- **Vulgate (v. 58):** renders it "Antequam Abraham fieret, Ego sum" (before Abraham was made, I am). — https://biblehub.com/commentaries/john/8-58.htm

**What I couldn't find:**

- Methodist, Pentecostal, Lutheran or Orthodox readings.
